slots.practicalActivity: In the Azure portal, create a real Azure Databricks workspace resource (Premium or trial tier), then launch it and land on the workspace home page. Take a screenshot-free tour just by clicking through: note the region, the pricing tier, and the Azure resource group it created alongside the workspace.
slots.deliverable: A live Azure Databricks workspace in your own Azure subscription, confirmed reachable at its workspace URL, with the resource group and pricing tier noted in a short setup log.

slots.practicalActivity: Tour every left-nav area of the workspace (Workspace, Catalog, Workflows, Compute, SQL), then use the real "Create compute" form to build a small all-purpose cluster: pick a policy, set autoscaling to 1-2 workers, and set automatic termination to 30 minutes so it never bills idle.
slots.deliverable: One running all-purpose cluster with autoscaling (1-2 workers) and a 30-minute auto-termination configured, visible as RUNNING on the Compute page.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new notebook named nyc_taxi_explore, attach it to the cluster from the previous slot, and write at least three cells mixing languages with magic commands: a %python cell loading a small sample file, a %sql cell querying it, and a %md cell documenting what each does.
slots.deliverable: A saved notebook with at least one %python, one %sql, and one %md cell, all successfully executed against the attached all-purpose cluster.

lessons.title: Attaching a Notebook to a Cluster

slots.practicalActivity: Detach the notebook from its cluster and reattach it to confirm state resets, then upload a small NYC Taxi CSV sample into DBFS using the Catalog > Upload File UI, and browse it from a notebook cell with %fs ls /FileStore/.
slots.deliverable: An uploaded NYC Taxi CSV sample visible under DBFS, confirmed with a successful %fs ls listing and a notebook cell that reads the file's first few rows with spark.read.csv().

slots.practicalActivity: Add a dbutils.widgets.text widget for a vendor_id filter to the nyc_taxi_explore notebook and use its value inside a %python filter expression, then run spark.version and check the cluster's Databricks Runtime version against the Compute page's configuration.
slots.deliverable: A notebook cell that filters the taxi sample using a widget-driven value (re-run with at least two different widget values to confirm it works), plus a one-line note recording the cluster's exact Databricks Runtime version.

lessons.title: Databricks CLI and REST API Basics

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Job in Workflows that runs the nyc_taxi_explore notebook on a daily schedule using a job cluster, then install the Databricks CLI locally, configure authentication with a personal access token, and run `databricks clusters list` and `databricks jobs list` from your terminal.
slots.deliverable: A scheduled Job visible in Workflows (with its job-cluster config), plus terminal output from the Databricks CLI successfully listing your clusters and jobs.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Databricks Fundamentals: without new instruction, build one small end-to-end artifact from scratch combining this chapter's pieces — a new cluster with autoscaling and auto-termination, a parameterized notebook using a widget, and a scheduled Job that runs it — then trigger the Job manually once and confirm it completes successfully.
slots.deliverable: One new cluster, one widget-parameterized notebook, and one scheduled Job that has been manually triggered and completed successfully at least once, all created without re-watching any lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Load the NYC Taxi sample into a DataFrame and write it out twice: once as plain Parquet and once as a Delta table (df.write.format("delta").saveAsTable("trips")). Use %fs ls on both output folders to see the extra _delta_log directory the Delta version has.
slots.deliverable: Two tables built from the same source data — a plain Parquet table and a Delta table named trips — with a short note comparing their folder contents, specifically the presence of _delta_log.

slots.practicalActivity: Append a second batch of trip rows into the trips Delta table, then run DESCRIBE HISTORY trips and open one of the raw JSON commit files under _delta_log with %fs head to see the actual add/remove actions Delta recorded for that write.
slots.deliverable: DESCRIBE HISTORY output showing at least two commits on the trips table, plus the raw contents of one _delta_log JSON commit file pasted into a notebook markdown cell with a one-sentence explanation of what it records.

slots.practicalActivity: Try to append a DataFrame with an extra column (e.g., a derived trip_duration_min column) into the trips table and capture the schema-mismatch error, then retry the same write with .option("mergeSchema", "true") so the table evolves to include the new column.
slots.deliverable: A captured schema-enforcement error message from the first failed write, followed by a successful second write (with mergeSchema) proven by DESCRIBE TABLE trips now listing the new trip_duration_min column.

slots.practicalActivity: With the trips table now at several versions from earlier slots, query an older version two different ways: SELECT * FROM trips VERSION AS OF 1 and SELECT * FROM trips TIMESTAMP AS OF '<a timestamp from DESCRIBE HISTORY>', comparing row counts against the current version.
slots.deliverable: Two time-travel queries (VERSION AS OF and TIMESTAMP AS OF) each run successfully against the trips table, with their row counts compared in a markdown note to the current version's row count.

slots.practicalActivity: Run an UPDATE to zero out any negative fare_amount rows, a DELETE to remove rows with a null trip_distance, and then a real MERGE INTO upsert that applies a small batch of "corrected" trip rows (some matching existing trip_id values, some new) into the trips table in one atomic statement.
slots.deliverable: Confirmed results of all three operations: zero negative fares after UPDATE, zero null-distance rows after DELETE, and a MERGE INTO run that both updated at least one existing row and inserted at least one new row, verified by querying the affected trip_id values before and after.

slots.practicalActivity: Check the current small-file count under the trips table's folder, run OPTIMIZE trips ZORDER BY (VendorID) to compact them, then run VACUUM trips RETAIN 168 HOURS (dry run first with DRY RUN) to preview which obsolete files would be removed.
slots.deliverable: A before/after file-count comparison showing OPTIMIZE reduced the number of small files, plus a VACUUM DRY RUN output listing the obsolete files that would be deleted under the default retention period.

slots.practicalActivity: Delta Lake chapter lab: build one fresh Delta table from a new NYC Taxi batch and run the full lifecycle on it end to end in order — create, append, evolve the schema, run a MERGE upsert, query an older version with time travel, then OPTIMIZE and VACUUM (dry run) — without re-watching any lesson.
slots.deliverable: One Delta table that has been created, appended to, schema-evolved, merged into, time-traveled against, and optimized/vacuumed, with a short log recording each step's command and result.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch the bronze/silver/gold layers you'll build for a NYC Taxi pipeline, then create the bronze layer for real: land a fresh batch of raw taxi CSV files into a bronze Delta table exactly as they arrived, with no cleaning or type casting.
slots.deliverable: A one-paragraph medallion design sketch for the taxi pipeline, plus a real bronze_trips Delta table holding the raw, unmodified ingested rows.

lessons.title: The Silver Layer — Cleaned and Conformed Data

slots.practicalActivity: Build a silver_trips table from bronze_trips that casts types correctly, drops duplicate trip_id rows, and removes clearly invalid fares, then build a gold_daily_revenue table that aggregates silver_trips into daily total revenue and trip counts by VendorID.
slots.deliverable: A silver_trips table with correct types and no duplicate trip_id values, and a gold_daily_revenue table whose totals you've spot-checked against a manual SQL GROUP BY on silver_trips.

slots.practicalActivity: Turn the two manual builds from the previous slot into reusable notebooks: a bronze_to_silver notebook that can be re-run against any new bronze batch, and a silver_to_gold notebook that recomputes gold_daily_revenue from the current state of silver_trips.
slots.deliverable: Two parameterized notebooks — bronze_to_silver and silver_to_gold — each re-run successfully a second time against newly added bronze data, with gold_daily_revenue reflecting the new totals.

slots.practicalActivity: Replace the manual bronze ingestion with Databricks Autoloader: configure a cloudFiles stream pointed at a DBFS folder of taxi CSV files, run it once to ingest existing files, then drop a brand-new CSV into that folder and re-run to confirm Autoloader picks up only the new file.
slots.deliverable: An Autoloader-based ingestion into bronze_trips that, on a second run after a new file is dropped into the source folder, ingests only that new file's rows — confirmed by comparing row counts before and after.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a basic Structured Streaming job using spark.readStream to read from the Autoloader source and spark.writeStream to continuously append into bronze_trips, running it in the notebook and watching the streaming query's progress metrics update live.
slots.deliverable: A running (or recently stopped) Structured Streaming query writing into bronze_trips, with at least one screenshot-free note of the batch progress metrics (rows processed, processing time) observed in the notebook's streaming dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert the bronze_to_silver notebook into a streaming job reading from bronze_trips and writing into silver_trips, then add a withWatermark on the event timestamp column so a deliberately late-arriving test row is still handled correctly instead of silently dropped or duplicated.
slots.deliverable: A streaming bronze-to-silver job with a watermark configured, proven by injecting one deliberately late-timestamped row and confirming it lands correctly in silver_trips exactly once.

lessons.title: Data Quality Checks in the Medallion Flow

slots.practicalActivity: Add explicit data quality checks into the bronze-to-silver step: reject rows with a negative fare_amount or null VendorID into a separate quarantine_trips table instead of silently dropping or allowing them into silver_trips.
slots.deliverable: A quarantine_trips table that captures rows failing the quality checks, confirmed by seeding a few deliberately bad rows and verifying they land in quarantine_trips, not in silver_trips.

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble everything built in this chapter into one orchestrated run: Autoloader into bronze, the streaming bronze-to-silver job with watermarking and quality checks, and the silver-to-gold aggregation, triggered in sequence against the same source folder.
slots.deliverable: A single documented run log showing bronze, silver, and gold tables all refreshed in sequence from one new batch of source files, with row counts recorded at each layer.

slots.practicalActivity: Medallion Architecture chapter lab: without new instruction, stand up a complete bronze-silver-gold pipeline from scratch against a different NYC Taxi file set than the one used in lessons, including Autoloader ingestion, a watermarked streaming silver step, a quarantine table for bad rows, and a gold aggregate — then run it twice to prove the incremental behavior works.
slots.deliverable: One original, independently built medallion pipeline (bronze/silver/gold plus quarantine) run successfully twice against a new file set, with row counts at each layer recorded for both runs.

slots.practicalActivity: Check whether your workspace is Unity Catalog-enabled, then browse the Catalog explorer and identify the three-level catalog.schema.table namespace for an existing table, writing out the full three-level name for one table built earlier in this course.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed Unity Catalog-enabled workspace with the full catalog.schema.table three-level name written down for at least one table created in an earlier chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new catalog (e.g., nyc_taxi_catalog) and a schema inside it, then create one managed table and one external table (pointing at a specific cloud storage path) inside that schema, and DROP each one to observe the difference in whether the underlying data files are deleted.
slots.deliverable: One catalog and schema containing a managed table and an external table, with a recorded observation of which table's data files disappeared after DROP TABLE and which did not.

slots.practicalActivity: GRANT SELECT on the gold_daily_revenue table to a test group, confirm it worked by checking SHOW GRANTS, then apply a column mask to redact a sensitive column (or a row filter restricting rows by VendorID) using Unity Catalog's row/column security functions.
slots.deliverable: A GRANT confirmed via SHOW GRANTS, plus a working column mask or row filter on a table, demonstrated by querying the table as a role without the unmask privilege and seeing the restricted result.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Lineage tab for gold_daily_revenue and trace it back through silver_trips to bronze_trips, confirming the chapter's medallion pipeline shows up correctly, then create a Unity Catalog Volume and copy a non-tabular file (e.g., a PDF or image) into it to see governed file storage outside of Tables.
slots.deliverable: A lineage graph screenshot-free walkthrough note confirming bronze -> silver -> gold traces correctly, plus a Unity Catalog Volume containing one uploaded non-tabular file.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Delta Share containing the gold_daily_revenue table and generate a recipient activation link (even without a real external recipient, walk the share-creation flow through to completion), then audit your own catalog setup against a Unity Catalog best-practices checklist (naming, least-privilege grants, managed vs. external usage).
slots.deliverable: A created Delta Share containing at least one table, plus a short written audit of your catalog's naming conventions and grants against best practices, with at least one concrete fix applied.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Unity Catalog: without new instruction, create a brand-new catalog/schema from scratch, migrate one of this course's existing tables into it as a managed table, apply a real GRANT to a test group, and verify the table's lineage shows correctly in the new location.
slots.deliverable: A new catalog/schema containing one migrated managed table with an active GRANT and a verified lineage view, built independently without re-watching any lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Lakeflow (Jobs & Pipelines) area of the workspace and explore the Lakeflow Connect ingestion connector gallery, then configure one simple connector-based ingestion (or a file-based Lakeflow Connect source if no external system is available) pointed at your NYC Taxi source files.
slots.deliverable: A configured Lakeflow Connect ingestion source visible in the workspace, with a short note on which connector type you used and why it fit the taxi data source.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline notebook and define a bronze_trips_dlt table with @dlt.table reading from the Autoloader source, then a silver_trips_dlt table built from it with @dlt.view intermediate steps, running the pipeline and watching the dependency graph render.
slots.deliverable: A running Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline whose dependency graph shows a bronze table feeding a silver table through at least one @dlt.view step, confirmed successful in the pipeline's run UI.

slots.practicalActivity: Add an @dlt.expect_or_drop rule to the silver_trips_dlt table rejecting rows with a negative fare_amount, run the pipeline in Triggered mode once to confirm it, then switch the same pipeline to Continuous mode and watch it keep running against new arriving files.
slots.deliverable: The pipeline's data quality metrics showing at least one row dropped by the expectation rule, run successfully in both Triggered mode (single run) and Continuous mode (left running against the source folder).

slots.practicalActivity: Wrap the Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline in a Lakeflow Job that triggers it on a schedule, then open the pipeline's event log and monitoring view to review the per-table update history, data quality metrics over time, and any flagged anomalies.
slots.deliverable: A scheduled Lakeflow Job that successfully triggers the declarative pipeline at least once, plus a written summary of what the event log and monitoring view showed for that run (tables updated, rows processed, quality metrics).

lessons.title: Course Recap — From Storage to Orchestrated Pipelines

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short comparison table of Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines vs. traditional Azure Data Factory pipelines (orchestration model, where transformation logic lives, monitoring), then walk back through every table, job, and pipeline built across this course's five chapters and list them in one inventory document.
slots.deliverable: A written Lakeflow-vs-ADF comparison table, plus a complete inventory listing every cluster, table, catalog, and pipeline artifact built during this course.

slots.practicalActivity: Course capstone lab: build one complete, governed Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline from scratch over a fresh NYC Taxi batch — bronze ingestion via Lakeflow Connect/Autoloader, a silver table with at least one expectation rule, a gold aggregate registered under a Unity Catalog catalog/schema with a real GRANT applied, orchestrated by a Lakeflow Job and verified in the monitoring view.
slots.deliverable: One original end-to-end governed pipeline — Lakeflow Connect/Autoloader ingestion, an expectations-checked silver table, a gold aggregate under Unity Catalog with an active GRANT, and a scheduled Lakeflow Job — run successfully at least once and documented in a short portfolio write-up.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After completing this course, a student can provision and operate Azure Databricks clusters and notebooks, build and manage Delta Lake tables with ACID transactions, schema evolution, time travel, and MERGE upserts, design and run streaming bronze/silver/gold medallion pipelines with Autoloader and data quality checks, govern data with Unity Catalog access control and lineage, and build, orchestrate, and monitor declarative pipelines in Lakeflow.
